name: LedisDB
tagline: Redis-like data-structure server in Go that keeps data on disk via LevelDB, RocksDB or goleveldb.
description: LedisDB, started by Siddon Tang in 2014, implements Redis-style KV, list, hash, set and sorted-set commands in Go but persists them to an embedded disk engine (goleveldb, LevelDB, RocksDB or an in-memory backend), so datasets are not limited by RAM. It speaks enough of the Redis protocol to be managed with redis-cli and many Redis clients, adds an HTTP API with JSON/BSON/msgpack output, Lua scripting, TTLs, master-slave replication and repair tools, and can be embedded as a Go library; clustering relied on the separate xcodis proxy. It was a popular 'Redis on disk' option in China around 2015-2017. The last tagged release is v0.6 (2017) and the last commit was in May 2020; the repository is not archived but is effectively unmaintained.
statusNote: No commits since May 2020 and no release since v0.6 (Nov 2017); not formally archived. Kvrocks or Pika are maintained disk-backed Redis alternatives.

scale.notes: Disk-backed so datasets can exceed RAM; sharding via the separate xcodis proxy.

strengths: Redis data structures without the RAM limit, persisted to LevelDB/RocksDB
Manageable with redis-cli and many existing Redis clients
Embeddable as a Go library or run as a server
weaknesses: Only a subset of Redis commands and semantics
Clustering needs an external proxy; replication is asynchronous
useCases: Existing deployments that need disk-backed Redis-style structures
Reference for mapping Redis types onto an LSM store
notIdealFor: New projects (use Apache Kvrocks, Pika or Redis/Valkey)
